subject: VPC routing questions and action log
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finserv.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap & open network asks from today's discovery call

Alex — thanks for the time today. High-level recap and the specific network items we need to qualify Private VPC for FinServ: 

Summary (from call)
- FinServ preference: Private VPC (data residency + audit controls) over Hosted API or Dedicated capacity.
- Primary cloud: AWS (us-east-1). Secondary: planned GCP for DR.
- Traffic pattern: steady low-latency inference for customer-facing APIs, peak spikes during batch jobs.

Open networking questions / decision points (please confirm):
1) Connectivity type: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering. Which is allowed by your security policy? PrivateLink provides cross-account ENI and avoids route table changes, peering requires CIDR planning.
2) Egress/static IPs: Do you require static outbound IP(s) for our service endpoints (e.g., allowlist on your firewall)? If so, please provide preferred IP ranges or confirm that an allowlist of our furnished set is acceptable.
3) Subnet/CIDR: Please provide at least one subnet CIDR we can use for routing/peering and any reserved ranges we should avoid.
4) Ports/protocols: We primarily require outbound HTTPS (443) to our control plane and inbound/outbound connections for model traffic if peered — list any blocked ports.
5) Cross-account IAM/roles: Will FinServ create an AWS role for us to assume for validation steps, or do you prefer we use an external bastion + NetOps coordination?

Attachments: I attached the "rwd-connect-reqs-20261101.xlsx" pack with recommended CIDR templates, PrivateLink endpoints, and minimal firewall rules. Also attached the NDA you signed for reference.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You: confirm connectivity choice (PrivateLink vs Peering) and provide a contact in NetOps with CIDR and firewall owner.
- Us (Ben + Marissa): produce a preflight checklist and a short runbook for your NetOps team. Target: deliver preflight within 48 business hours after your network confirmation.
- Schedule: recommended 60–90 day target for go-live once we finish network testing and compliance checks.

If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute technical workshop with our L3 network engineer to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0199

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finserv.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@finserv.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap & open network asks from today's discovery call

Aisha — great summary, appreciate it. A few clarifications from our side (NetOps copied):

1) Connectivity: Our security policy forbids cross-account ENIs for third parties, so PrivateLink is a no-go for now. We need VPC Peering (cross-account) or a managed transit approach.

2) Static egress IPs: Yes, we require static egress IPs for upstream telemetry and control calls. We cannot add dynamic ranges to the allowlist. Please provide a small set (<= 4) of IPs or an AWS-managed elastic IP approach.

3) Ports: 443 outbound to your control-plane endpoints is approved. We also allow inbound TLS (443) from peered CIDRs if required for your worker pools. No other ports are open by default.

4) CIDR guidance: We can provision a /24 for this integration (10.40.12.0/24). Please confirm that this works, and we'll create a peering request once we have your account ID and proposed route table entries.

5) Timeline: procurement needs a SOW + cost estimate before we commit to creating peering. Procurement (copied) — can you start the SOW intake?

Let's get a 30-minute engineering sync Tues 11/2 10am ET if that works.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Platform Engineering — FinServ Inc.
alex.j@finserv.io | +1 617-555-0133

Subject: Internal: FinServ peering asks & internal engineering checklist

Aisha / Marissa — quick internal note after Alex's reply. Key items for Eng/Pre-sales to action:

- Static IPs: Engineering should confirm whether we can publish up to 4 elastic IPs in AWS for control-plane egress, or if we need to propose a NAT/proxy architecture. If we cannot guarantee static IPs in the customer's region, call that out in the SOW as a blocker.
- Peering flow: Prepare steps for cross-account VPC peering request, required account IDs, and route table change notes. Add rollback guidance in case of overlapping CIDRs.
- Security/compliance: Marissa to confirm SOC2 artifacts we will link in the SOW and preflight; procurement will need them.
- Cost delta: Provide a rough cost delta between Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) vs Private VPC (network egress + peering), include 12-month TCO.

Action owners / ETA:
- Ben: produce a short engineering appendix (peering + elastic-IP options) — due 2026-11-02 EOD PT.
- Marissa: bundle SOC2 + compliance note for procurement — due 2026-11-03.
- Sean: join Tue 11/2 sync and be prepared to discuss capacity and cost tradeoffs.

I'll draft the SOW template language once Ben confirms the IP approach.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

1) Meeting: Confirming Tue 11/2 10am ET for the technical sync (we'll send calendar invite). Ben and Sean will join for network/capacity discussion.
2) IP list: Ben will circulate proposed elastic IP set in advance of the call (attachment: rwd-connect-reqs-20261101.xlsx). If NetOps prefers an AWS-managed NAT with fixed IP, note that in the sync.
3) Preflight: We'll provide a preflight pack with specific route entries and minimal firewall rules in that spreadsheet. Please upload any internal network diagrams to the shared Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d-finserv-onboarding
4) Procurement ask: Procurement — please start the SOW intake. We will attach SOC2 evidence and the compliance appendix (Marissa will send).

Please reply with: the primary NetOps contact (name + email) and the procurement PO owner so we have direct lines. Looking forward to the sync.
